parts.problem_md: Do you think businesses should prioritise ethical practices over profit maximisation? **Justify** your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Businesses may prioritise profit maximisation over ethical practices because ethical sourcing and fair labour practices require higher operational costs **[K]**. This reduces profit margins and may make products less competitive on price **[An]**

However, businesses that ignore ethical practices risk facing consumer boycotts **[K]**, as customers increasingly demand transparency and ethical behaviour from companies. This could lead to significant revenue losses and damaged brand reputation **[An]**

Businesses should consider that whilst prioritising profit may provide short-term financial gains, unethical practices can result in legal penalties and regulatory sanctions **[E]**. Furthermore, companies that maintain strong ethical standards often build greater customer loyalty and attract socially conscious investors, ultimately creating sustainable long-term profitability **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) → 1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Higher costs of ethical sourcing [k] leading to reduced profit margins [an]
>   - Shareholders expect maximum returns [k] so ethical spending may reduce dividends [an]
>   - Competitors may gain cost advantages [k] by avoiding ethical investments [an]
>   - Fair trade certification costs are expensive [k] reducing funds available for expansion [an]
>   - Consumer demand for ethically produced goods [k] can increase sales revenue [an]
>   - Risk of boycotts from socially conscious consumers [k] leading to loss of customers [an]
>   - Government incentives for ethical practices [k] can offset implementation costs [an]
>   - Strong ethical reputation attracts quality employees [k] reducing recruitment and retention costs [an]
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - Yes, businesses need to prioritise profit to survive and satisfy shareholders [k] as ethical investments increase operational costs [an].
>   - However, ignoring ethical practices damages brand reputation [k] leading to lost customers and potential legal issues [an].
>   - The long-term benefits of ethical practices, including customer loyalty and regulatory compliance, often outweigh short-term profit losses, so businesses should balance both priorities. [eval] [eval]

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**Everyone Theatre (ET) **

Zane and Zaara are both actors. They plan to start up a theatre in a low-income area of Main City. Zane and Zaara believe that helping the community is as important as being successful entrepreneurs.

The theatre will be a private sector business and Zane and Zaara have to decide whether to start up as an unincorporated business (partnership) or as a limited company. Zane is planning to prepare a cash-flow forecast for the first year. Zaara knows they will need to set business objectives for the theatre and also decide on a leadership style to use when managing employees. ET will have 24 part-time employees as shown in the organisational chart in Appendix 1.

Zane and Zaara plan to put on performances in the evenings for local people and tourists. There will be 100 seats in the theatre but not all the seats will be sold if the price is too high. The Marketing Manager, Zaara, will need to decide which performances to put on, what price to charge and which refreshments to sell. Zaara will also need to decide between the two possible options for the first performance when the theatre opens. Information on the two options is shown in Appendix 2.

In the daytime the theatre building will be used by Daycare, a local social enterprise. Daycare takes care of young children up to the age of 5 so that low-income family members can go out to work. It also provides education for the children which helps their development and progress before they start school. Some of Daycare’s objectives are different to those of ET

**Appendix 1 **

**Proposed organisational chart for the theatre**

Note: The numbers in brackets are the number of part-time employees who work in each department

**Appendix 2 **

**Forecast data for the two possible options for ET’s first performance at the theatre**

| For each performance | **Option 1** | **Option 2** |
|---|---|---|
| Number of actors/employees | 7 | 24 |
| Average wage cost per actor/employee | \$30 | \$10 |
| All other costs including scenery, costumes and promotion | \$1000 | \$2000 |
| Forecast revenue assuming all 100 seats are sold | \$1000 | \$2500 |

**Appendix 3 **

**Email from Zane to Zaara**

**To: Zaara **

**From: Zane **

**Date: 1 April 2023**

We want to support the local community and we need to make decisions about the following.

Should we:

- Pay fair wages even though they may be higher than those paid by competing theatres?
- Only buy costumes produced in the local community?
- Purchase all refreshments from suppliers that do not pollute the environment?

Consider the following **three **ethical issues for the theatre.

- Paying fair wages to employees
- Only buying costumes produced in the local community
- Purchasing all refreshments from suppliers that do not pollute the environment

Which ethical issue is likely to have the biggest effect on ET? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/jun-2023-paper-2-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Paying fair wages to its 24 part-time employees **[Ap]** would increase ET's costs significantly. This could force ET to increase ticket prices, potentially reducing demand and revenue. However, fair wages may motivate employees to work harder, improving the quality of performances and attracting more customers **[An]**

Only buying local costumes would support the community, aligning with Zane and Zaara's goal. This could generate goodwill and attract more local customers to fill the 100 seats **[Ap]**. However, costume quality may be lower, impacting performance quality **[An]**

Purchasing eco-friendly refreshments shows environmental responsibility but may limit choices and be more expensive. This could slightly reduce refreshment sales **[Ap] **if increased costs are passed on to customers, though these are a minor part of ET's total revenue **[An]**

In conclusion, fair wages will likely have the largest financial impact on ET's costs and potential revenues **[E]**. It also most directly affects ET's 24 employees and the local community, making it the ethical issue with the biggest overall effect on the theatre's operations and success **[E]**. As ET is in a low-income area of Main City **[Ap]**, fair wages could boost the local economy and increase people's ability to afford theatre tickets **[Ap]**, further boosting ET's reputation **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Paying fair wages to employees**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Provides local people with higher incomes → raises living standards → expands pool of customers able to buy theatre seats → revenue up
>     - Higher wages boost staff motivation → better performance quality → stronger audience satisfaction
>     - Reduces turnover among 24 part-timers → builds loyalty → cuts recruitment and training costs
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Wage bill increases → higher operating costs → may force up ticket prices → risk of lower attendance
>     - Price-sensitive patrons may be priced out → potential drop in revenue
> - **Only buying costumes produced in the local community**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Showcases local craftsmanship → attracts community support → ticket sales rise
>     - Generates positive publicity → word-of-mouth promotion → longer-term audience growth
>     - Creates local jobs → boosts area’s standard of living → strengthens theatre’s social impact
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Local suppliers may lack specialist skills → costume quality could suffer → harms production standards
>     - Limited local capacity → supply delays or inconsistencies → operational risk
> - **Purchasing refreshments from environmentally friendly suppliers**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Aligns with sustainability goals → appeals to eco-conscious patrons → improves brand image
>     - Reduces likelihood of pressure-group protests → creates a more welcoming environment for tourists
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Ethical suppliers often charge premiums → refreshment profit margins fall → lowers ancillary income
>     - Smaller supplier pool → limited snack/drink variety → may disappoint some customers
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Fair wages impose the largest cost increase and could require higher ticket prices, posing the greatest risk to attendance and profit
>   - Local costumes strengthen community ties and publicity but may compromise quality if skills are lacking
>   - Eco-friendly refreshments support reputation with relatively small cost impact
>   - overall, paying fair wages is likely to have the greatest effect on the theatre’s finances, while green refreshment sourcing has the least financial impact but still bolsters reputation

**Extract:** **MainCity Bakery (MB)** MainCity Bakery (MB) MB is a small bakery that produces bread. Yasin started the bakery 6 months ago with help from the government. Yasin needed a business plan to support his application for government help. An extract from the business plan Yasin produced is shown in Appendix 1. The market research was carried out by Yasin. He asked a small sample of family and friends to fill in a questionnaire. Yasin’s business plan also contained forecast data. MB’s bread is freshly-made every day in the bakery, which is located at the back of MB’s small shop. The bread is then sold the same day. Yasin has 2 employees to help him produce the bread and 1 employee to serve customers in the shop. All employees work 5 days a week and are paid the legal minimum wage. Yasin uses a democratic leadership style. Yasin needs to keep costs low to be competitive. He uses packaging that cannot be recycled. Yasin also buys the cheapest ingredients, most of which are imported. He is planning to use lean production in the bakery but he has to decide which method to use. MB’s main competitors advertise that they only use ingredients from local suppliers. Yasin is thinking of changing the suppliers he uses for ingredients and packaging. He wants MB to have a good ethical image which he could use in advertising. Yasin plans to start making cakes. He is considering two options as outlined in Appendix 2. MB’s fixed costs will increase as there will be additional expenses whichever option he chooses. **Appendix 1 ** **Extract from Yasin’s business plan for MB** | Section | Details | |---|---| | Market research | Questionnaire results are as follows:

- Bread is eaten by all age groups
- Of the sample asked:
- 85% want products made using ingredients from local suppliers
- 70% want to purchase cakes as well as bread from a bakery | | Resources | - \$10 000 to buy bakery equipment
- Rent for the bakery and shop each month
- \$3000 for start-up supplies and ingredients | **Appendix 2** **Forecast data for MB’s cake options** | | **Option 1 Small cupcakes** | **Option 2 Large birthday cakes** | |---|---|---| | Monthly sales of cakes | 4000 | 100 | | Variable cost per cake | \$0.50 | \$10 | | Additional fixed cost per month | \$3000 | \$3000 | | Price per cake | \$2 per cupcake | \$60 per birthday cake | | Gross profit margin | 75% | 83.33% | | Sales growth | Low | High | **Appendix 3 ** **Packaging supplier advertisement** We only supply packaging made from sustainable sources. This will keep your products fresh and protect the environment. We can deliver your packaging when you need it. Consider the following **three **ways Yasin could improve the ethical image of MB. - Buying all ingredients from local suppliers. - Using only environmentally friendly packaging. - Increasing wage rates to 20% above the legal minimum wage. Which way would be most effective? **Justify **your answer. Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/jun-2022-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
By switching to local suppliers, MB could compete directly with rivals on their ethical stance. It aligns with Yasin's desire to develop an ethical image **[Ap]** and, as 85% of people surveyed want products made using local ingredients **[Ap]**,  it would be very popular with customers and could significantly boost MB's image and sales. It is likely, though, to be more expensive than buying cheaper, imported ingredients **[An]**

Currently, MB uses packaging that cannot be recycled **[Ap]**, which is not sustainable. Switching to eco-friendly packaging would reduce waste and appeal to environmentally conscious customers **[An]**, and there is an available supplier of sustainable packaging **[Ap]**. However, this might increase costs and some customers may not notice the change in packaging **[An]**

Increasing wages to 20% above the legal minimum could improve employee motivation and reduce staff turnover within the bakery **[Ap]**. This could lead to better quality products, indirectly improving MB's image **[An]**. However, it would increase costs significantly and may not be as visible to customers as the other options **[An]**

Overall, the improved ethical image and ability to compete with local rivals on social responsibility could justify the higher costs of local ingredients **[E]**. Sourcing locally offers the best balance of meeting customer preferences, matching competitor strategies, and creating a visible ethical stance **[**`equation`E**]** for customers of bakery products** [Ap]**. This approach is most likely to enhance MB's reputation and attract environmentally conscious customers than the other options **[**`equation`E**]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Buying all ingredients from local suppliers**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Ingredients sourced locally → no imports → lower transport pollution and carbon footprint
>     - Supports local businesses (e.g. flour mills) → strengthens community relations
>     - Cheaper and quicker deliveries → fresher ingredients and lower logistics cost
>     - Meets customer demand (85 % surveyed prefer local sourcing) → aligns with market preferences
>     - Matches competitor practices → no loss of competitive position
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Local ingredients cost more than low-cost imports → may require higher selling prices → risk of reduced demand
>     - Limited supplier range → potential constraints on product variety and recipe flexibility
> - **Using only environmentally friendly packaging**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Enhances bakery’s green image → appeals to eco-aware consumers and new market segments
>     - Future-proofs against stricter environmental regulations → reduces compliance risk
>     - Reliable sustainable packaging supplier available (Appendix 3) → ensures continuity
>     - Lowers risk of activist or pressure-group backlash → protects reputation
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Eco-friendly packaging may offer less product protection → risk of damaged goods
>     - Time spent sourcing new packaging → less focus on core baking operations
>     - Higher packaging costs (likely 10 %+ increase) → may force price hikes → some customers may resist
> - **Increasing wages to 20 % above the legal minimum**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Better pay → higher employee motivation and productivity
>     - Lower staff turnover → savings on recruitment and training
>     - Stronger employer brand → easier to attract and retain quality workers
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Wage bill increases → higher operating costs → profit margins under pressure
>     - If competitors match pay rises → loses motivational advantage
>     - Pay policy may not be widely known → limited impact on public reputation
> - **Recommendation**
> 
>   - Local sourcing delivers environmental and community benefits but needs a pricing or volume strategy to offset higher input costs
>   - Sustainable packaging boosts the bakery’s green credentials and regulatory resilience yet demands careful cost management to retain price competitiveness
>   - Above-minimum wages foster staff loyalty and productivity but should be clearly communicated to amplify reputational gains without eroding margins

parts.problem_md: Do you think a business being ethical will always lead to lower profits? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Some customers may be prepared to pay extra for ethical products or ethical company behaviour** [K]**. This can help offset the increased costs of using ethically-sourced materials, for example, **[An]** so overall profit margin may not change**,** and the better reputation gained could result in additional sales** [An]**

However, some firms may struggle to find ethically-sourced raw materials, especially locally** [K]**. The long delivery distances and extra transport costs **[An]** may push prices so high that demand is reduced** [An]** and profits fall

Therefore, being ethical can benefit a business, as in the long term revenue** **and profits may increase ** [E]**. However, some customers may not be prepared to pay the higher price for the ethical behaviour, particularly for everyday low-cost items **[E] **so profits are likely to fall

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Enhance reputation/brand image [k] helps attract customers [an]
>   - Customers may pay higher prices [k] increasing revenue / which could help cover the costs [an]
>   - Can help motivate employees [k] increasing productivity / reduces absenteeism / lowers labour turnover [an]
>   - Can increase costs [k] leading to higher prices [an] which may lead to fewer customers / sales [an]
>   - May not be sufficient materials / difficult to find ethical suppliers [k] reducing output [an]
>   - Ethical suppliers may have higher prices / unethical suppliers may be cheaper [k]
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - Some customers may be prepared to pay extra for ethical products [k] this can help offset the increase costs of trying to be ethical [k] so overall profit margin may not change [an] and the better reputation gained could result in additional sales [an]. Therefore, being ethical can benefit a business as in the long term this may increase revenue [eval] which could result in higher profit overall [eval]

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> ACP manufactures computers. Being ethical is important to ACP. The business employs 3000 workers in its factory. ACP imports 65% of its raw materials. As internal users of accounts, the directors plan to analyse ACP’s financial performance using profitability ratios. The Finance Director thinks making a profit is more important for a business than managing its cash flow.

Explain **one **benefit and **one **limitation to ACP of being ethical.
parts.solution_md:
If ACP is considered ethical,** **it will likely have a good reputation** [K]** and this will generate strong loyalty** **from customers, who may be more willing to pay high prices **[An] **for its computers **[Ap]**

However, ACP may have limited choice of sources of materials  from abroad** [Ap]** as it will be difficult to inspect suppliers for ethical behaviour** [K]**. This may lead to lower levels of quality **[An] **

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Write two developed paragraphs, one for each part of the question
> - For each paragraph:
> 
>   - State a valid point relevant to the question → 1 K mark
>   - Apply it clearly to the business in the case study → 1 Ap mark
>   - Explain the impact using a cause–effect chain → 1 An mark
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Benefits:
>   
>     - Good image/good reputation/customer loyalty [k] so customers more willing to pay high prices [an] for its computers [app]
>     - High/higher demand/sales [k] which can help increase revenue [an]
>     - Can help recruit/motivate/retain workers [k] reducing recruitment costs [an] as the business has 3000 employees [app]
>     - Better supplier relations (as pay a fair price) [k] which can help ensure the necessary supply to maintain production [an]
>     - Investors more likely to invest [k]
>     - Less opposition from pressure groups [k]
>   - Limitations:
>   
>     - Limited/fewer sources of materials [k] which may lead to less output [an] as already imports 65% of its raw materials [app]
>     - May have to pay more to suppliers [k] leading to higher variable costs/cost of goods sold [an]
>     - Workers may have to be paid more [k] at the factory [app] increasing labour costs [an]
>     - Higher costs [k] could lead to higher prices [an]
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
> - The following words are likely to be appropriate for this question:
> 
>   - 65%/import
>   - Cash flow
>   - Raw materials
>   - Computers
>   - 3000 employees
>   - Factory
>   - Production/manufacture
>   - Profit is important/profitability ratios
